```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(TrajectoryMarkovAnalysis)
```

The package has two independent estimation paths. One estimates transitions
from recorded patient histories. The other allocates recorded costs to those
histories. A model can use either set of estimates, or probabilities and costs
supplied from other sources. Every value below is synthetic.

## Prepare histories and estimate transitions

Each row describes an inclusive dated interval for one patient. The analyst
defines the clinical states and identifies any absorbing states. Patient IDs
are preserved, including character IDs.

```{r histories}
paths <- list(
  p1 = c("Stable", "Complication", "Dead"),
  p2 = c("Stable", "Stable", "Complication", "Dead"),
  p3 = c("Stable", "Complication", "Complication", "Dead"),
  p4 = c("Stable", "Stable", "Stable", "Stable")
)
trajectories <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(paths), function(id) {
  start <- as.Date("2026-01-01") + 7 * (seq_along(paths[[id]]) - 1)
  data.frame(subject_id = id, state_label = paths[[id]],
             state_start_date = start, state_end_date = start + 6)
}))
histories <- prepareTrajectories(
  trajectories, cycleLength = 7, absorbingStates = "Dead"
)
fitted <- estimateTransitions(histories)
fitted$estimates
```

Transition denominators contain observed adjacent-cycle pairs. A final
censored interval does not imply that the patient stayed in the same state.
Unsupported rows remain missing, and projection stops if it reaches an
unsupported row. Declared absorbing states have structural identity rows.

Use `periodBreaks` and `periodLabels` to estimate different follow-up periods.
Use `strata` for recorded covariates, with `addCovariateGroups()` when continuous
values need explicit categories. Each transition belongs to the source row's
period and covariates. A patient can therefore contribute to several age groups.

## Allocate costs separately

Local cost records need a patient ID, date and amount. Missing amounts remain
missing. The package does not infer a currency or convert prices automatically.

```{r costs}
records <- data.frame(
  subject_id = c("p1", "p1", "p2", "p3", "p4"),
  event_date = as.Date("2026-01-01") + c(0, 7, 0, 7, 0),
  amount = c(100, 250, 100, 200, 100),
  currency_concept_id = "44818568", measure = "total_charge"
)
costs <- estimateStateCosts(histories, records)
costs$estimates
```

For a connected study, `extractCosts(cdm, histories, ...)` reads costs through
a database-backed `CDMConnector` reference. The caller creates and closes the
connection. The `visitFilter` argument can select visit IDs, visit concepts,
or visits linked to specified clinical concepts. Duration allocation spreads
an amount over its original inclusive service interval and reports shares
outside the observed histories. Use `adjustCostPrices()` with a supplied
price index when amounts span price years.

## Declare event order when the study needs it

An end-of-week state cannot reveal whether a complication preceded death
within that week. Supply explicit stage observations to
`estimateStageTransitions()` when those events are observed. Supply matrices
to `composeTransitionStages()` when the stage probabilities come from an
external source or a defined scenario.

Here onset operates first and mortality second. The intermediate event remains
available even when both happen in one cycle.

```{r stages}
states <- c("Stable", "Complication", "Dead")
onset <- matrix(c(.9, .1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1), 3, byrow = TRUE,
                dimnames = list(states, states))
mortality <- matrix(c(.98, 0, .02, 0, .9, .1, 0, 0, 1), 3, byrow = TRUE,
                    dimnames = list(states, states))
model <- composeTransitionStages(
  list(onset = onset, mortality = mortality), cycleLength = 7,
  absorbingStates = "Dead"
)
effect <- list(prevention = list(
  stage = "onset", from = "Stable", to = "Complication",
  multiplier = .75, redistributeTo = "Stable", endDay = 28
))
reference <- projectCohort(model, nCycles = 52, initial = c(Stable = 1),
                          cohortSize = 1000)
intervention <- projectCohort(model, nCycles = 52, initial = c(Stable = 1),
                             cohortSize = 1000, transitionEffects = effect)
```

The multiplier is a supplied intervention assumption. An observed association
between complication and mortality does not establish that prevention would
remove that mortality difference.

## Use the same accounting for expected and sampled outcomes

State costs below are amounts per weekly interval. `costTiming = "onset"`
charges the post-onset state, including the last living interval before death.
Health outcomes use the state at interval start. Other timing choices must be
specified explicitly.

```{r rewards}
rewards <- function(program_cost) createRewardModel(
  stateCosts = c(Stable = 10, Complication = 30, Dead = 0),
  upfrontCosts = c(program = program_cost),
  aliveStates = c("Stable", "Complication"),
  utilities = c(Stable = .8, Complication = .6, Dead = 0),
  costTiming = "onset", healthTiming = "start", discountTiming = "midpoint",
  costDiscountRate = .035, healthDiscountRate = .035,
  currency = "EUR", priceYear = 2026
)
reference_outcomes <- summariseOutcomes(reference, rewards(0))
intervention_outcomes <- summariseOutcomes(intervention, rewards(15))
comparison <- compareScenarios(reference_outcomes, intervention_outcomes)
comparison$costEffectiveness
```

A 52-step weekly projection has 52 completed intervals, totalling 364 days.
The final snapshot does not add another interval. The separate
`projectCosts()` and `summariseSimulation()` functions use their documented
full-label convention. Do not mix those summaries with interval summaries.

A model bundle can simulate individual paths, update time-varying covariates
between steps, and resume later with `advanceSimulation()`. Its private random
stream avoids changing the caller's random seed.

```{r simulation}
sampled <- simulateTrajectories(
  createModelBundle(model), n = 100, initial = c(Stable = 1), nSteps = 12,
  terminalStates = "Dead", transitionEffects = effect, seed = 192
)
summariseOutcomes(sampled, rewards(15), nCycles = 12)$totals
```

An explicitly longer accounting horizon is permitted only after all patients
have reached declared absorbing terminal states. It adds terminal snapshots,
not new events or living time. These paths illustrate fixed-input sampling
variation. They are not estimates of intervention-effect uncertainty.

## Extend mortality only with explicit inputs

`createMortalityTransitions()` accepts supplied background probabilities.
`calibrateExcessMortality()` matches that background to the observations that
contributed to each fitted mortality estimate. `extrapolateMortality()` can
then use a specified handover, background model and excess-hazard rule.
Unsupported ages, covariate combinations and future periods cause errors unless
the analyst supplies an explicit extension. The package does not download a
life table, assume an old-age rate, or establish the validity of the extrapolated
tail.

Results and simulations can contain individual records. No export or disclosure
policy is applied automatically. Review the returned tables before sharing them.
